Understanding Decimal Numbers:
🔴 Understanding Decimal Numbers 🔴

Decimals are a special way to write numbers that are smaller than a whole!

1. What is a decimal number?

A decimal number uses a decimal point (a little dot) to separate the big whole-number part from the tiny fractional part. For example, 3.5 means 3 whole units, plus half of another unit!

2. Decimals represent fractions

Decimals are just another way to write fractions with denominators like 10, 100, or 1,000! Imagine a chocolate bar divided into 10 pieces. If you eat 5 pieces, you ate 5 tenths of the bar. 5/10 is exactly the same as 0.5!

3. Decimals in everyday life

Decimals are everywhere! We use them for money (like $2.75), measuring length (a pencil is 12.5 cm long), and measuring weight (a bag of flour weighs 1.5 kg).
Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths:
🔍 Tenths, Hundredths & Thousandths 🔍

Let's zoom in on the tiny pieces past the decimal point!

1. Slicing the Whole

  • Tenths: Divide one whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth (0.1).
  • Hundredths: Divide one whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is one hundredth (0.01).
  • Thousandths: Divide one whole into 1,000 equal parts. Each part is one thousandth (0.001).

2. How zeros affect value

Zeros are very important placeholders! 0.8 means eight tenths, but 0.08 means eight hundredths. Those are very different amounts of cake! But, adding zeros to the very end doesn't change anything: 0.5 is exactly the same as 0.50.
Place Value in Decimals:
🏠 Place Value in Decimals 🏠

Every digit has its own special spot in the number house!

1. Face Value vs. Place Value

Face value is just the digit itself (like the 5 in 4.58). But its place value depends on where it sits! In 4.58, the 5 sits right after the decimal point, so its place value is 5 tenths (0.5).

2. Expanded Form

Expanded form breaks a number apart to show what every single digit is worth. The number 4.58 can be written as: 4 + 0.5 + 0.08!

3. Moving Digits

Each place is ten times bigger than the place to its right. 0.4 is four tenths, 0.04 is four hundredths. Every time a digit moves one step to the right, it becomes ten times smaller!
Reading and Writing Decimals:
🗣️ Reading and Writing Decimals 🗣️

How to speak decimal language perfectly!

1. How to read them

There are two ways to read 12.45:

  • Digit by digit: "Twelve point four five". (Never say "point forty-five"!)
  • Using place value: Read the whole number, say "and" for the decimal point, read the rest like a normal number, and say the name of the very last place! "Twelve and forty-five hundredths."

2. Matching places to words

The final decimal place tells you the name!

  • One decimal place (0.7) = Tenths (Seven tenths)
  • Two decimal places (0.24) = Hundredths (Twenty-four hundredths)
  • Three decimal places (0.125) = Thousandths (One hundred twenty-five thousandths)
Comparing and Ordering Decimals:
⚖️ Comparing & Ordering Decimals ⚖️

Which decimal is the true heavyweight champion?

1. The Golden Rule of Comparing

Compare the big whole numbers first! 4.7 is bigger than 3.9 because 4 is bigger than 3. You don't even need to look at the decimals!

2. The Zero Trick

If the whole numbers are the same, things get tricky. Is 0.7 bigger or smaller than 0.65? 65 looks bigger than 7, right? WRONG!

To compare them fairly, they need the same number of decimal places. Add a zero to the end of 0.7 to make it 0.70. Now compare: 70 hundredths is bigger than 65 hundredths! So, 0.7 > 0.65.

3. Ordering

Ascending order means smallest to largest. Descending order means largest to smallest. Always use the Zero Trick before you put them in order!
Converting Fractions to Decimals:
🔄 Fractions to Decimals 🔄

Changing a fraction's disguise into a decimal!

1. The Easy Denominators

If the bottom number is 10, 100, or 1,000, you have it easy! Just look at the top number and put it in the right place value.

  • 3/10 = 0.3 (Three tenths)
  • 32/100 = 0.32 (Thirty-two hundredths)
  • 8/100 = 0.08 (Eight hundredths. Don't forget the zero placeholder!)

2. Equivalent Fraction Magic

If you have a fraction like 1/2, the bottom number isn't a 10. But we can make it one! Multiply the top and bottom by 5, and it becomes 5/10. Now we can easily write it as 0.5!

3. The Division Method

A fraction is just a secret division problem! 1/4 literally means 1 ÷ 4. If you divide 1 by 4, you get 0.25!
Converting Decimals to Fractions:
🔄 Decimals to Fractions 🔄

Turning decimals back into fraction puzzle pieces!

1. Place Value Tells All

To turn a decimal into a fraction, look at the last digit's place value!

  • One decimal place: 0.2 is two tenths, so write it as 2/10.
  • Two decimal places: 0.75 is 75 hundredths, so write it as 75/100.
  • Three decimal places: 0.125 is 125 thousandths, so write it as 125/1000.

2. Don't forget to simplify!

Once you write your fraction, you should simplify it to its lowest terms! For 0.6, we write 6/10. Both 6 and 10 can be divided by 2, so the final simplified answer is 3/5!
Addition and Subtraction of Decimals:
➕ Subtracting & Adding Decimals ➖

The most important rule in all of decimal math!

1. Line up the Dots!

When adding or subtracting decimals, there is one golden rule: ALWAYS LINE UP THE DECIMAL POINTS! Write the numbers one below the other so that the dots form a perfectly straight vertical line.

2. The Zero Trick (Again!)

What if you need to add 3.5 + 2.36? They don't have the same number of digits! Simple: Add a placeholder zero to the end of 3.5 to make it 3.50. Now it's easy: 3.50 + 2.36 = 5.86.

3. Borrowing and Carrying

Once your dots are lined up, you just add or subtract exactly like you would with normal whole numbers! If a column adds up to 10 or more, carry the 1. If you can't subtract a big number from a little number, borrow from the next column to the left!
Multiplication and Division of Decimals:
✖️ Multiplying & Dividing Decimals ➗

Making decimals multiply and split!

1. Multiplying by a whole number

Multiplication is just repeated addition! 1.2 × 3 is the same as saying 1.2 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 3.6.

💡 Quick Method: To solve 1.2 × 4, ignore the decimal point for a second. 12 × 4 = 48. Since 1.2 has one digit after the decimal, put the decimal one spot from the right in your answer: 4.8!

2. The 10 and 100 Slide

Our number system uses place value! Multiplying a decimal by 10 makes its value ten times larger (all digits slide one place left). Dividing by 10 makes it ten times smaller (all digits slide one place right).

  • 2.4 × 10 = 24
  • 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5
Rounding Decimals:
🎯 Rounding Decimals 🎯

Finding a friendly, nearby number!

1. What is rounding?

Rounding means replacing a number with a nearby, simpler number. For example, a length of 4.8 meters is approximately 5 meters when rounded to the nearest whole number.

2. The Bossy Neighbor Rule

To round a number, find your target place value, then look at the bossy neighbor digit immediately to its right!

  • 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4: Keep your target digit the exact same! (Round down).
  • 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9: Boost your target digit up by 1! (Round up).

3. Examples

Round 3.42 to the nearest tenth. The tenths digit is 4. The bossy neighbor to the right is 2. Since 2 is small, we keep the 4! The answer is 3.4.

Round 6.8 to the nearest whole number. The whole number is 6. The bossy neighbor to the right is 8. Since 8 is big, we boost the 6 up to 7!
Decimal Word Problems:
🕵️‍♂️ Decimal Word Problems 🕵️‍♀️

Solving real-world mysteries with money, distance, and weight!

1. Choosing the right operation

Decimal word problems are just like normal word problems. You have to read the clues to pick the right operation!

  • Combining quantities: Addition (e.g., 2.5 L + 1.2 L)
  • Finding what remains: Subtraction (e.g., 6.0 kg − 2.4 kg)
  • Repeating equal quantities: Multiplication (e.g., 1.5 m × 4)
  • Sharing equally: Division (e.g., 4.8 L ÷ 6)

2. Multi-step problems

Some problems require more than one step! If Alex buys a bag for $12.75 and a bottle for $3.60, and pays with a $20 bill, how much change does he get?

First, add the total cost: 12.75 + 3.60 = 16.35. Then, subtract that from the money he gave: 20.00 − 16.35 = $3.65 in change!
